title: SourceInventory
description: Canonical source inventory (organize v3 / taxonomy scheme_version 4). It preserves native/deterministic extraction provenance, separates raw text from LLM-assisted proposals, and links each derived sidecar to an access-controlled original. v3 adds the open-world signals the closed 14-domain scheme could not carry: `kind` (known | novel | unreadable), `clinical_class` (the enum downstream gates key off — a novel molecular panel filed under 15_ still trips the molecular completeness gate), `doc_kind`, `text_layer_kind`, `novel_reason`, `reread_channel` and `transcript_path`. It is not an authorization record, not a claim of anonymity, and `kind: unreadable` NEVER means the material is covered — it must surface in readiness.json.projection_coverage.

scheme_version.description: Bucket-taxonomy scheme this inventory was written against (references/bucket_taxonomy.json). It must be DECLARED: an archive that omits the key is not a legacy archive, it is an archive that did not say, and the validator ERRORs asking for `scheme_version: 4` (or 3 for a genuine pre-v4 archive). Treating silence as 3 was the hole — every v4-only gate skipped itself on any inventory that simply forgot the key, so the cheapest way to pass the open-world floors was to delete one line. An explicit 3 still stays READABLE: the validator relaxes the v4-only requirements, WARNs, and points at scripts/migrate_v3_to_v4.py. 4 is the current scheme and is validated in full — there is no forward-compatible value beyond it. Rows using 15_ / open sub-buckets are only meaningful under scheme 4.

patient_dir.description: Relative path or placeholder for <patient_dir> (e.g. "." or the patient-dir basename) — not an absolute path, so the inventory stays portable and never leaks a host filesystem path. All relative paths below resolve under this directory.

file_id.description: Stable id of this content unit (1:1 with the sidecar/MD), e.g. f001. N content units may share one source_id when a single upload yields multiple sidecars. See bucket-taxonomy.md §4.

source_id.description: Stable per-upload id, e.g. s001. 1:1 with an uploaded original in raw/; N content units may share it.

original_path.description: De-identified raw handle (the 段 1 de-id raw filename / source_id) recorded for audit; never used as an anchor. MUST be relative/de-identified — never a host-absolute path (/Users/...), cloud URL, email-attachment path, OR an identity-bearing upload basename (e.g. NOT '张测试-报告.pdf'). The verbatim upload filename is preserved only in raw/_FILENAME_MAPPING.md (inside raw/, excluded from export). source_inventory.json is a delivered/shared surface; the delivered-surface PII rescan (pii_rescan.py) hard-fails name/path leaks here.

raw_path.description: Protected relative path to the uploaded original. Access requires host authorization; the path is never an anchor or an export default.

page_range.description: Which pages of a multi-document source this content unit covers, e.g. "3-5". Null when the sidecar covers the whole file.

kind.description: Open-world classification of this content unit. `known` = fits a pinned doc type under domains 01_..14_. `novel` = real medical/administrative material no pinned domain fits; it is filed under 15_未分类资料/<slug>/ and REQUIRES novel_reason. novel is NOT quarantine: it is never auto-deleted, never demoted to 99_无关文件 (which holds only likely_unrelated material), and its clinical_class still drives the molecular/lab completeness gates. `unreadable` = the source could not be transcribed (illegible, encrypted, opaque binary); it MUST NOT be counted as covered by any patient-facing surface and MUST appear in readiness.json.projection_coverage.

doc_kind.description: Document type name. For kind=known, a pinned doc type name (e.g. "NGS报告", "出院小结"). For kind=novel, the form `novel:<slug>` where <slug> satisfies bucket_taxonomy.json open_sub_bucket_slug_regex and misses reserved_sub_bucket_names — it is written by a model from untrusted source text, so it is validated, never trusted. Replaces the legacy free-form `doc_type` key, which was never in this schema; gates read doc_kind and fall back to doc_type for old archives.

clinical_class.description: What KIND of clinical content this unit carries, independent of where it was filed. This is the key downstream consumers and the completeness gates read — NOT the bucket path — so a novel gene-panel report sitting in 15_未分类资料/ still trips the molecular gate instead of silently producing an empty molecular.json. It is a routing signal, NOT a diagnosis: `pathology` says the document IS a pathology report, never what it concluded. Use `unknown` only when the material genuinely resists classification; `unknown` on a source whose transcript contains lab values or variants is a defect.

novel_reason.description: REQUIRED when kind=novel: why no pinned domain fits, in the organizer's own words, citing what the document actually is. Blocks the failure mode where 15_ becomes a silent dumping ground — every open-world filing decision stays auditable.

text_layer_kind.description: Nature of the PDF/page text layer, decided by scripts/prepare_pages.py, not by a model. `born_digital` = real embedded glyphs from the producing application — the text layer IS the character truth and a vision disagreement goes to discrepancy[] instead of overwriting it. `embedded_ocr` = a text layer exists but the page is a full-page image (a scanner's own OCR), so the text layer is a second CHANNEL, never the truth. `absent` = no text layer; pixels are the truth. `not_applicable` = the unit has no page raster at all (plain text, CSV, structured payload).

transcript_path.description: Relative path to the VERBATIM per-page transcription for this unit, e.g. raw/transcript/<source_id>/page-001.md. REQUIRED for any unit that was transcribed. It lives under raw/ on purpose: it is unmasked character truth, it inherits raw/'s host access control, it is NEVER loaded into a downstream context, and scripts/export_share.py refuses it. The masked sidecar (sidecar_path) is the only downstream-readable surface.

legacy_transcript_unavailable.description: TRUE only on a row that scripts/migrate_v3_to_v4.py carried forward from a scheme-3 archive whose characters a model read (read_mode model_vision_primary / model_vision_assist) at a time when no per-page transcript was written. Such a row CANNOT produce a transcript_path — the pages were never transcribed to disk and re-reading them would be a new run, not a migration — so the transcript_path requirement and gate_transcripts are relaxed for it. What it does NOT buy is coverage: the row MUST be counted in readiness.json.projection_coverage.summary.unreadable_sources and the archive MUST carry a review_flag with category coverage_gap / audience internal_qc, because 「we cannot re-check this source」 is exactly the fact a coverage number exists to surface. Never set it on a row a v4 run produced: there it would be a transcript the run simply declined to write.

bucket_path.description: Canonical bucket-relative path of the text-masked .md SIDECAR after 段 2 classification (clinical domain 01_…14_). The original is NOT copied here — it stays once in raw/ (see raw_path). Null before classification or for isolated unrelated files.

sidecar_path.description: Bucket-relative source-attributed, text-masked MD sidecar. The leading NN_ bucket segment is required.

modality.description: Orthogonal data-nature tag (independent of the clinical-domain bucket) driving ingest-parser dispatch. text=prose/OCR doc; image=imaging/scan stub; structured=tabular numeric report; omics_raw=parseable omics payload (VCF / annotated TSV / expression-methylation matrix); timeseries=wearable/PRO/longitudinal stream → longitudinal_observations.json; binary_other=opaque/unsupported binary, incl. BAM/FASTQ/DICOM/proprietary (stub + [INGESTION_BLOCKED], never silently dropped). See bucket-taxonomy.md §2 and ingest-adapters.md.

read_mode.description: Primary character-extraction mode for this content unit. `model_vision_primary` (organize v3) is the honest label for a pixel page (text_layer_kind absent | embedded_ocr) whose character truth IS the multimodal transcription — use it instead of mislabelling such a page deterministic_ocr/hybrid_verified. Declaring it does NOT relax the high-risk rule: every high-risk field (references/high-risk-fields.md) still needs a CHANNEL-INDEPENDENT second read before high_risk_review_status may become passed_independent_reread. `native_text` is reserved for born-digital text taken byte-for-byte from the source — the only mode eligible for faithfulness_method: native_text_identity.

raw_output_ref.description: Protected relative reference to preserved native/OCR character output; never a public export default.

llm_role.description: What the LLM actually did for this unit. `primary_transcription` (organize v3) records that a model wrote the character truth for a pixel page — a provenance admission, not a quality claim, and never by itself a substitute for the independent reread.

high_risk_review_status.description: Status of the CHANNEL-INDEPENDENT second read for identifiers, dates, drug/dose/frequency, laboratory values/units/reference ranges, stage, variants/VAF and accession numbers (references/high-risk-fields.md). `passed_independent_reread` is legal ONLY when reread_channel is present and is not `none`, and that channel is genuinely independent of the first read: a different model, a different modality (born-digital text layer, barcode decode, a parseable deterministic OCR run), or a human. Re-prompting the SAME model on the SAME image — including a cropped region — is a tie-break only and never sets this value. Disagreement → needs_human_review with both reads recorded side by side; majority voting is forbidden.

transcribe_model_id.description: Identifier of the model that produced the FIRST read (段 1 transcription) for this unit, e.g. "host-vision-3.0". REQUIRED in practice for any unit whose read_mode is model_vision_primary / model_vision_assist, because independence of the second read is otherwise uncheckable: without a first-read model id, `reread_channel: alternate_vision_model` is an unfalsifiable claim. null only for units no model transcribed.

high_risk_fields.description: PER-FIELD second-read record for this unit's high-risk fields (references/high-risk-fields.md: identifier, date, drug_name, dose, frequency, lab_value, unit, reference_range, accession + the oncology pack stage, variant, vaf). The row-level high_risk_review_status is a DERIVED summary of this array (any needs_human_review → needs_human_review; all passed → passed_independent_reread; empty → not_applicable) and the gate checks the derivation. Recording the channel per FIELD is what makes the claim checkable: one field verified through a born-digital text layer says nothing about the handwritten dose beside it.

label.description: The field label AS THE SOURCE PRINTS IT, matching the transcript frontmatter fields[].label it came from.

status.description: Outcome for THIS field. passed_independent_reread requires reread_channel ∉ {none} and a genuinely independent channel; disagreement is never voted away — it becomes needs_human_review with both readings kept in readings[].

reread_channel.description: The independent channel that supplied this field's second read. `text_layer` is legal ONLY when the unit's text_layer_kind is born_digital or not_applicable (a deterministic adapter's output for a non-raster unit). embedded_ocr and absent are excluded: there the “text layer” is the same pixels read twice, not an independent channel. `alternate_vision_model` REQUIRES reread_model_id ≠ transcribe_model_id. `human` REQUIRES a matching verdict in raw/_provenance/<run>/human_sample_result.json — it is never a no-channel placeholder. `none` means no second read happened, and then status must not be passed_independent_reread.

reread_model_id.description: Model that performed the second read. REQUIRED (non-null) and MUST differ from transcribe_model_id when reread_channel is alternate_vision_model — re-prompting the SAME model on the SAME image, including a crop, is a tie-break and never an independent channel.

readings.description: Every reading of this field, one per channel, kept side by side. On disagreement BOTH survive here — majority voting is forbidden and the reviewer must see what each channel actually said.

channel.description: Which channel produced THIS reading. `transcribe` is the 段 1 first read (the multimodal transcription itself); the other five are the independent second-read channels and match reread_channel's vocabulary minus `none`. `none` is deliberately absent here: 「no second read happened」 is the ABSENCE of a second readings[] entry, not a reading whose channel is nothing — recording it as one made an unverified field look like a verified one with an odd label. One writer of this array (scripts/ingest_transcripts.py) and two readers (the validator, references/high-risk-fields.md §2.4) share this exact list; a sixth spelling of the first read — `first_read`, `model_vision_primary` — is a schema violation, because a channel name nothing matches is a channel nothing checks.

value.description: The value as that channel read it, verbatim.

reread_channel.description: Row-level SUMMARY of the primary independent channel across this unit's high_risk_fields[]. `none` means no independent second read happened — in that case high_risk_review_status must NOT be passed_independent_reread. `human` is NOT a no-channel placeholder: declaring it requires a matching verdict in raw/_provenance/<run>/human_sample_result.json, so 「人工看过」 can never be asserted without the record that proves it. `text_layer` is legal only when text_layer_kind is born_digital or not_applicable — never embedded_ocr or absent, where the “text layer” is the same pixels read twice (schema allOf). `deterministic_ocr` counts only when the OCR run actually parsed: tesseract is tri-state — 0 bytes / garbage = NO signal and raises no flag; parseable + a numeric-level conflict on a high-risk field = trigger a second read; agreement = a confidence bonus. It never vetoes on its own.

adapter.description: Format adapter used to make the source extractable and independently reviewable; it does not create a new clinical source.

adapter_provenance.description: Short provenance such as decode_tool=sips;rotation=90 or pdftoppm pages=3. Temporary paths are allowed only as provenance, never as anchors.

persist.description: Whether this source file is selected for final archive/persist. Medical sources cited by formal outputs (timeline/case_text/review outputs/structured JSON source_refs) must be true; false is reserved for isolated unrelated/non-persisted sources.

allOf.$comment: Open-world filings must justify themselves: kind=novel without novel_reason is a schema error, so 15_ can never become an unaudited dumping ground.

A unit whose characters came out of a model MUST record where the verbatim per-page transcription lives. Omitting transcript_path used to skip gate_transcripts entirely (its three assertions all short-circuit on an absent path), so 'no transcript declared' was cheaper than 'transcript declared and checkable'. The ONE exemption is legacy_transcript_unavailable: true, which only scripts/migrate_v3_to_v4.py may write — a scheme-3 row whose pages were read by a model before per-page transcripts existed cannot produce a file that was never created, and demanding one would make every pre-v4 archive permanently unmigratable. The exemption is paid for elsewhere: gate_projection_coverage counts such a row as unreadable and requires a coverage_gap flag.

The gate excludes exactly two values, embedded_ocr and absent, because those are the cases where the 'text layer' is not independent of the first read: with absent there is no text layer at all, and with embedded_ocr it is a scanner's own OCR of the very pixels the model looked at. born_digital is the classic legal case (real embedded glyphs from the producing application). not_applicable is legal too and is NOT an oversight: a unit with no page raster — a VCF, a DICOM header, a timeseries payload — has its characters produced by a deterministic adapter, and that adapter output IS a channel independent of any vision read.
